page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7a.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 architecture. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 32 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. It operates on a KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a 16 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmarks indicate strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng scores placing it in the top 25% of tested hardware. The CPU architecture supports AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instructions, contributing to strong cryptographic and extended instruction performance in PassMark tests. Memory performance is mixed; small-block cached read bandwidth is exceptionally high, whereas large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the average range. The instance demonstrates strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and high-throughput Redis SET operations, alongside strong prompt processing and text generation for small language models. However, medium model LLM inference speeds are average, and large model inference is unsupported by the hardware profile.

Given its compute-heavy 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and lack of bundled local storage, the ecs.c7a.16xlarge offers high resource density for CPU-bound tasks without the overhead of local disk maintenance. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring high parallel processing power rather than massive memory footprints or local NVMe storage. Best-fit workloads include multi-threaded decompression, database operations, high-throughput Redis caching, ray tracing, image processing, and small-scale LLM inference.
